title: Quarterly Surge-Control & Model Curation Playbook for Hosted Endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a repeatable quarterly playbook that aligns hosted endpoint release lanes with model catalog curation, capacity surge controls, and compute budget hedges. The playbook should enable PMs and SREs to coordinate canary windows, trunk rotations of model variants, and emergency fallback policies while keeping token-unit economics predictable. Scope: hosted endpoints (all tiers), model variant lifecycle (add/retire/quantize), canary scheduling, surge capacity triggers, and runbook for degraded-model fallbacks. Out of scope: Dedicated contractual negotiation and private on-prem rollout automation (handled by a follow-up workstream).
acceptance_criteria: Published playbook doc in Confluence with step-by-step quarterly cadence
Cross-functional calendar templates (canary windows, freeze periods, capacity hedges) created and shared
Model compatibility matrix produced for top 10 hosted models mapping latencies and memory footprints
SRE-run surge-policy implemented behind feature flag (capacity_burst_v1) and validated in staging
Two dry-run rehearsals completed with on-call rotation and incident simulation
tasks: Draft initial cadence and decision checkpoints (PM lead)
Workshop with Runtime and Infra to define surge thresholds and fallback model variants
Assemble model compatibility matrix and perf profiles (Research/Applied ML)
Design canary calendar template and guardrails for rollbacks (Console UX + Eng)
Create Confluence playbook + checklist and link to runbook runbooks and dashboards
Implement feature-flagged surge-policy in staging (ENG-52314) and run integration tests
Schedule two cross-functional rehearsals and capture lessons learned

risks: Large-model memory spikes during canaries could invalidate surge thresholds
Cross-team scheduling friction during end-of-quarter freezes may delay rollouts
Incomplete compatibility mappings could lead to subtle behavior/regression between variants
Customer-facing latency regressions if fallback policies are too aggressive
decisions: Adopt a three-lane surge policy: normal, hedge, emergency. Each lane maps to explicit model variant families and token-budget caps
Canary windows will be scheduled in the first two weeks of each quarter with a 48-hour observation period
Fallback routing will prefer quantized-compatible variants where available to minimize cost impact
SRE will own the final go/no-go for escalations; PMs will own stakeholder comms
